description:
M27 - Our team combines planetary research and software development. We are dedicated to improving space exploration, combining research, data analysis, and software development to help for preparation for the future human missions to the Moon and Mars.

Team:

Kristína (Slovakia) - Project lead, gathers and analyzes scientific information, focuses on design, presentation

Martin (Czechia) - Develops the functional Mission Analog website, turning data into an interactive app
summary:
Mission Analog is an interactive app designed to identify the most suitable places on Earth for testing future Moon and Mars missions. 

We have developed two demonstrators:
One is focused on lunar environments and another on Mars, using Arcadia Planitia as a reference for a future human base and resource extraction (ISRU).

We compared terrain, temperature, sunlight, ice resources, dust and environmental conditions by processing NASA and other scientific datasets.

Mission Analog ranks potential Earth analog sites using adjustable scores based on mission requirements and explains which conditions still require specialized simulations.
This helps identify and evaluate Earth locations that can support the preparation of future space missions. 

This project might be important because it helps scientists and engineers test technologies, understand environmental challenges and reduce risks before sending humans to the Moon or Mars.
details:
Mission Analog

There are two interactive websites: one for the Moon and other for Mars. You can change mission priorities and see how the results and location rankings change.

Benefits:

  • it helps find places to test space equipment
  • reduces risks for future space missions
  • Makes complex scientific data more comprehensive

The main goal is to help prepare for safer  human missions to the Moon and Mars by finding suitable testing locations on Earth.

Tools and technologies we used:

  • HTML, Python
  • Geospatial data processing
  • Terrain analysis
  • Data visualization

Mission Analog focuses on finding locations with similar environment conditions, combines various Earth locations because there's no place that can recreate everything found on another planet.

We considered:

  • Terrain, elevation
  • Temperature, sunlight
  • Underground ice
  • Dust, dryness
  • Accessibility and suitability for experiments
  • Conditions that cannot be recreated naturally on Earth (low gravity, radiation)
